extracted.intended_audience: DoD contracting officers, A-76 study teams, acquisition professionals and installation managers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and lessons learned for planning, conducting, evaluating, and administering OMB A-76 competitive sourcing studies (PWS, cost comparisons, source selection, QASP, contract administration, protests, and program management). Targets DoD installations and acquisition/contracting personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish Acceptable Quality Levels (AQLs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishment of AQLs with a reasonable level of effort to be performed by the MEO or contractor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AQLs should be set at realistic, documentable levels; used by QASP and inspectors to determine compliance. Ensure AQLs are neither arbitrary nor beyond contract scope to avoid disputes and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct Performance Requirements Review before advancing PWS
rubrics_metrics.description: A Performance Requirements Review should be accomplished prior to moving ahead with other portions of the A-76 study, especially the Performance Work Statement (PWS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents a PWS that does not accurately reflect the actual work to be accomplished. Review early to avoid misalignment between MEO and contractor bids and prevent procurement set-asides and re-competitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inflating PWS to 'get well' staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: Government activities should not attempt to 'Get Well' by adding work requirements not currently being done to gain additional manpower through the A-76 process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding work can leave an MEO with insufficient personnel if it wins; do not assume additional manpower will be granted. Keep PWS aligned with existing work unless legitimately added and resourced.

rubrics_metrics.name: PWS: state what work is required, not how to do it
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid telling bidders how they should accomplish the work; instead, tell them what work is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If particular approaches are necessary, outline those requirements in Section L of the solicitation and include them as evaluation criteria in the Source Selection Plan. Preserve contractor/MEO flexibility except where method is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of skeleton/previous PWSs with caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Mixed guidance on reusing prior PWSs: do not blindly copy old PWSs; however, templates may be used as a jumping-off point and catalyst to complete the study on time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor any template to meet specific needs. Templates can aid mandated timeframes but avoid perpetuating inaccuracies or outdated requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involve contracting office personnel in PWS development
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel from the contracting office should be involved in the development of the PWS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting personnel provide critical knowledge of contract requirements that must be represented in the PWS and can help ensure solicitations and clauses are appropriate and enforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Database systems and government access to contractor data
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilize database maintenance systems capable of updating the PWS whenever changes in workload data occur; Government should be given access to contractor-collected data regarding work performed and level of effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include data access requirements in the PWS and relevant contract clauses so the Government can monitor and update workload figures during the review and performance phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide contract type early and base it on Performance Summary
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision as to the type of contract utilized should be based on the nature of work outlined in the Performance Summary; gain concurrence early.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deciding contract type early prevents having to change documents and ensures PWS and contracting documents are developed consistently with the selected contract form. Do not begin work on PWS and other contracting documents until contract type is decided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain accurate workload data to avoid excess work and change orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Accurate workload data are needed to prevent work requirements from exceeding workload figures outlined in the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excess work leads to change orders which can increase contract price. Use reliable workload capture and validation methods during the study and include mechanisms for updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop an in-depth Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP)
rubrics_metrics.description: The QASP is vital in both fixed-price and cost reimbursement contracts to control costs and ensure contractor performance meets specified levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use QASP to discover discrepancies in the PWS that could raise price. Quality inspectors should not arbitrarily select surveillance methods; rely on functional personnel expertise to decide surveillance methods. QASP must be comprehensive to enforce contract terms and performance levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section L must specify required proposal content and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Section L should include information as to what offerors should provide as part of their bid and standardize formats to facilitate evaluation by the SSEB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify what to include in technical proposals, require staffing charts showing proposed staffing levels and positions, and require that manning levels equate to proposed hours in the Cost Proposal to assist consistent evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require Past Performance Summary Matrix from offerors
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractors should provide a Past Performance Summary Matrix including vital information from similar contracts previously undertaken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matrix should include technical points of contact and data relating to past contract performance to support evaluation of offeror experience and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify SSEB members early and screen conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the Source Selection Evaluation Board (SSEB) must be identified early to prevent them from becoming 'tainted' by participation in the Management Study or Independent Government Cost Estimate; develop a list of personnel forbidden from serving due to conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early identification and conflict-of-interest screening preserves evaluation integrity. Maintain documented exclusion lists and follow FAR guidance on organizational conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish source selection criteria and include price realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands should formulate and publish source selection criteria to guide decisions; Section M should indicate that price realism will be used along with lowest price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make evaluation criteria transparent in advance. Explicitly state how price realism and other factors will be considered to reduce protest risk and ensure offerors understand award considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require and evaluate a phase-in/transition plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase-in of the contractor into the organization should be staggered over months; a final date should be set for contractor to assume full responsibility and any Government-Furnished Property (GFP). Phase-in plan should be a requirement in the solicitation and evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staggered changeover reduces disruption. Include phase-in requirements in solicitation and evaluate proposals' transition approaches to ensure smooth assumption of duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a Contract Administration Plan (CAP) tied to QASP
rubrics_metrics.description: A Contract Administration Plan should be developed for administration of the contract and include requirements to inspect in accordance with the QASP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting Officers should involve functional personnel to ensure the CAP is technically sound. CAP should define inspection responsibilities, frequencies, and authorities consistent with QASP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting officer must control improper inspections and associated liabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Administration of QASP must ensure the contractor meets AQLs and inspectors do not levy requirements or inspections beyond contract scope; the Contracting Officer is obligated to correct improper inspections or risk liability to reimburse contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inspectors impose additional requirements and the CO does not correct them, boards may obligate the Government to reimburse contractors for additional expenses. Maintain oversight and correct inspector overreach promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle differing site conditions carefully to avoid material breach
rubrics_metrics.description: When existing site conditions differ from those stated in the contract, the Government should exercise care to avoid material breach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both Government and contractor should reach mutually agreeable positions to 'get off on the right foot.' Proper handling preserves relations and minimizes appeals or disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture and disseminate lessons learned across commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Government employees and contractors supporting the A-76 study should be responsible for capturing lessons learned in writing and making that available to other commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A comprehensive lessons learned system aids DoD-wide improvement. GAO recommends Devoting resources to documenting and disseminating lessons and best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct cost comparisons per solicitation 'ground rules'
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency decisions to perform services in-house instead of contracting are reviewed to ascertain whether the agency followed the announced 'ground rules' for the cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting officers and A-76 teams must conduct cost comparisons in accordance with criteria established within the solicitation to withstand review and protests (Comptroller General precedent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation must provide sufficient information for intelligent competition
rubrics_metrics.description: A procuring agency must provide prospective bidders with information sufficient to enable bidders to compete intelligently and on a relatively equal basis; an IFB need not eliminate all uncertainties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address ambiguities in amendments and pre-bid conferences where feasible; however, some performance risk is inherent and offerors are expected to account for it in their bids. Balance detail and practical risk allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid evaluator conflicts of interest per FAR 9.504
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and evaluate potential organizational conflicts of interest early and avoid, neutralize, or mitigate significant potential conflicts before contract award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to address significant conflicts can render evaluations invalid and sustain protests. Staff evaluation teams consistent with regulatory guidance to ensure impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: When significant conflicts taint evaluation, re-staff and re-evaluate
rubrics_metrics.description: If evaluators have significant conflicts of interest (e.g., 14 of 16 evaluators under study), the evaluation is invalid and does not provide a proper basis for cancellation or award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rescind flawed cancellations/decisions, staff a technical evaluation team consistent with guidance, and reevaluate proposals to correct process defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure uniform, functioning cost accounting methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular does not prescribe methods for capturing and recording costs; commands need uniform and functioning cost accounting methods capable of providing accurate cost data quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands should establish consistent methods and systems for calculating direct, indirect, and G&A costs and for handling non-standard costs (volunteers, prison labor). Lack of uniformity lengthens and complicates studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize limits of A-76 'best value' and include past performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Circular A-76 allows for best value under modified conditions but lacks guidance on how past performance should be measured and incorporated into the cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include past performance data and a method to measure it where appropriate; clarify how past performance will factor into decisions to avoid ambiguity and protest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define inherently governmental functions and gray areas consistently
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no uniform DoD view on which functions are governmental vs commercial; commands should identify core inherently governmental functions and maintain lists of excluded activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize legal protections for certain services (e.g., fire, police, some depot maintenance) and document restriction lists to reduce ambiguity. Address 'gray area' functions through consistent policy and guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify common families of services suitable for competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain services are repeatedly opened for competition across Services and installations and may form a common family (e.g., base operating support, family housing management, base communications, utilities/heating, library services, base supply, grounds maintenance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cross-installation similarities to consolidate efforts, but recognize common services still require rigorous acquisition strategy and compliance with FAR to avoid protests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish strong management structure for A-76 studies
rubrics_metrics.description: A sound management structure (e.g., involvement of senior management, A-76 Council, or Integrated Product Team) is needed to meet timelines, resolve stakeholder conflicts, and develop a sound acquisition strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given complexity, consider quasi-program office approaches and full-time program managers to ensure studies complete on schedule and that budgetary expectations are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff A-76 teams appropriately, balancing full-time assignment and technical competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Installations should examine options for assigning A-76 study team members full-time; timelines are critical so full-time staff may be advisable though there is risk of losing touch with the studied functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign full-time members where necessary to meet timelines; maintain technical competence by involving functional personnel and ensuring knowledge transfer so staff remain current with the work being studied.
